subject: Agriculture
title: Community Supported Agriculture
description: A short lesson to help you apply Community Supported Agriculture.

hook.text: In CSA, consumers pay farmers upfront before the season starts. They share the risk and the produce.

buildup.text: Members receive weekly boxes of whatever's in season. Bad weeks mean less produce; great weeks mean abundance.

discovery.text: CSA eliminates the middleman. Farmers get 100% of the food dollar instead of the typical 15%.

twist.text: CSA serves committed consumers but reaches only a tiny fraction of food buyers—it doesn't scale easily.

climax.text: Over 7,000 CSA farms operate in the US—small in market share but large in cultural influence on food awareness.

punchline.text: Pay the farmer first. Share the harvest and the risk. Food becomes a relationship.

quiz.question: How much of the food dollar does a CSA farmer typically receive?

details.summary: Community Supported Agriculture connects consumers directly with local farms through subscription models where members pay upfront for weekly shares of seasonal produce. This topic explains how CSA works, its benefits, and its growth into a global movement.
details.whyItMatters: CSA reduces financial risk for small farmers, shortens supply chains, and reconnects communities with food production. It represents a fundamentally different economic model for agriculture based on shared risk and mutual benefit.
takeaways: CSA members prepay for seasonal farm shares, giving farmers guaranteed income
The model originated in Japan and Europe and now includes thousands of farms worldwide
CSA reduces food miles, packaging waste, and farmer financial risk simultaneously

faq.question: How does a typical CSA subscription work?
faq.answer: Members pay upfront at the start of the growing season for a weekly box of seasonal produce. This guarantees the farmer income regardless of market prices. Members share both the bounty of good harvests and the risks of crop failures.

faq.question: What are the main benefits of CSA for farmers and consumers?
faq.answer: Farmers get guaranteed upfront income, reduced marketing costs, and direct customer relationships. Consumers get ultra-fresh local produce, learn about seasonal eating, and develop connections to the land and the people who grow their food.
